title: The Gift I Became Too Careful About
scene: You go to buy a small birthday present for a friend and quickly find something suitable. Instead of buying it, you overthink what the gift might imply, compare several alternatives, and eventually return to the first option with less confidence than before.
sceneJa: 友人へのちょっとした誕生日プレゼントを買いに行き、最初の5分でよさそうなものを見つける。ところが『実用的すぎるか』『個人的すぎるか』と考え始め、候補を行き来した末、結局最初の品を以前より自信のない状態で買う。

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I was no longer choosing between presents / I was conducting / a surprisingly thorough risk assessment
I was no longer / choosing between / presents I was conducting a / surprisingly thorough risk assessment
I was / no longer choosing between presents I / was conducting a surprisingly / thorough risk assessment
questions.explanation: The first option keeps the contrast between the original activity and what it has turned into, then treats 'conducting a surprisingly thorough risk assessment' as one clear idea.

questions.question: What does ‘which should have made the whole trip very easy’ suggest?
options: Finding a suitable gift quickly should have meant there was little left to decide
The shop was difficult to get to
The speaker wanted to spend more time shopping
questions.explanation: The phrase sets up an expectation: the task ought to have been simple, but the speaker makes it complicated by overthinking.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence funny?
options: Because leaving a shop is presented as if it were an advanced skill
Because the friend returned the gift
Because the speaker forgot to pay
questions.explanation: The dry humour comes from describing a very ordinary act—buying something and leaving—as an advanced technique after unnecessary overthinking.

speak: Start with calm confidence. Let the pace become slightly more thoughtful through the practical-versus-personal dilemma. Read ‘a surprisingly thorough risk assessment’ with mock seriousness. Keep the friend's reaction short and ordinary, then deliver the final sentence very calmly, as if buying something and leaving really were an advanced method.
review: Recent daily-life lessons have covered a wrong-number phone call and a run derailed by coffee. Today shifts to gift shopping and overthinking. The flow is quick success → unnecessary doubt → escalating comparison → return to the first option → dry lesson. Useful chunks are ‘which should have made ...’, ‘I was no longer ...; I was ...’, and ‘go back to ...’.
